text:
maria: Quick follow-up from the offload refactor RFC — I sketched a smaller surface to reduce contention and fragmentation. idea: split 'admission' (should this allocation be offloaded?) from 'residency' (where we keep it) and make the allocator only responsible for leases, not policy.

kevin: can you sketch the call flow? curious about where we keep pinned vs staging state.

maria: call flow rough: app -> allocator.alloc() returns a Lease token. separate call: admission.admit(Lease, hints) -> returns {location: GPU|STAGING|RECOMPUTE, cost_hint}. allocator only tracks token->backing and free on release. admission service owns eviction decisions.

olga: splitting sounds nicer for testing, but careful: need a fast hot path for tiny tensors. can't add an RPC-like hop for every alloc.

maria: agreed. hot path idea: in-proc admission cache with fast-path decisions for small allocations and recent patterns. fallback to async policy thread for heavy decisions.

sam: what about fragmentation? if admission is separate, how do we prevent it from repeatedly moving small slabs and causing churn?

maria: two levers: 1) admission returns a frag_penalty estimate used by allocator to prefer coalescing-friendly placements, 2) lease-level tenure — newly offloaded pages start with probation tenure so we avoid immediate compaction.

kevin: frag_penalty sounds hand-wavy. need a concrete score and telemetry. e.g., per-allocation: {size, holes_created, expected_lifetime}. can we surface that in tracing?

maria: yes. telemetry plan: expose allocation events with fields: size, pool, frag_delta, admit_decision, tenure_deadline. we can add a small histogram in console.

olga: another tradeoff: prefetch vs recompute. for many small prompts recompute wins but admission needs a sigmoid that uses latency SLOs and token-cost.

sam: rollout plan? i'd prefer toggles per-tenant and a canary on Dedicated first.

maria: propose feature flags: offload.split_admit=true default:false, admit_cache_size=16k, probation_ttl=30s.

kevin: will this require allocator ABI changes? like new Lease token fields? we should avoid changing on-disk formats.

maria: minimal ABI change: Lease stays opaque string; we add a small "lease_flags" bitmask that allocator ignores except for eviction hints. allocator code only reads flags for coalescing heuristics (if present). No persisted format changes.

olga: nice. what about the staging pool sizing? we need adaptive sizing to avoid OOM storms.

maria: config prototype below:
```
offload.policy: "admit-by-free"
admit_threshold: 0.12
staging_pool_target: "0.15_total_vram"
admit_cache_size: 16384
probation_ttl_secs: 30
```

sam: runtime-bot flagged a CI perf test flake earlier — might be related to shadow admission cache. @runtime-bot can you paste the test log? :eyes:

runtime-bot: perf/test_offload_cache_cache_hit_rate flaky on mac-ci. last run: hit_rate=0.62 (expected >0.7). See logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/3456

kevin: that explains why we saw extra page churn in my local repro. cache size or eviction policy probably bad.

maria: OK action items: 1) formalize admit score (size, lifetime_hint, frag_delta) and add tracing fields, 2) implement in-proc admit cache with LRU+TTL, 3) probation tenure implementation in allocator, 4) perf CI tweak to stress small-tensor workloads.

olga: also add a test that simulates many small short-lived tensors to validate recompute vs staging thresholds.

sam: please add the feature flag + tenant rollout plan to the RFC follow-up doc. I'll take on the Dedicated canary checklist.

maria: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:

kevin: one more: let's add a metric for 'frag_penalty' distribution so SRE can alert on runaway fragmentation.

maria: added to the telemetry list. I'll push a short PR with the admit cache prototype tomorrow and ping for quick review.

olga: :rocket:

sam: sounds good.

maria: marking this thread as sync point — next checkin in 3 days or earlier if PR is up.
